population.note: FICTIONAL. One-line arithmetic: ever 37.8 − current 25.9 = 11.9 pts used-and-off; new ever-users 0.8 (0.6 on, 0.2 off); of the 27.9 on in 2032, 14.5 stayed on (52%, down from 60% because employers dropped coverage) and 13.4 stopped, joining 9.1 already off to make a pool of 22.5, of whom 10.8 restarted (48%, down from 57% because the pool now holds many coverage-loss and conditioning cut-offs), so on = 14.5 + 10.8 + 0.6 = 25.9 and off = 22.5 − 10.8 + 0.2 = 11.9; cycled = 13.4 (to 2032) + ~4.6 first-time restarters + ~0.1 among new starters = 18.1 of 37.8 = 48%. The 13.4 pts who stopped break down roughly as: employer coverage loss ~4.5, Bridge/Medicaid conditioning cut-offs ~2.5, GI and other side effects ~2.5, retatrutide users who reached goal and stopped or tapered ~1.5, and choice (backlash, litigation fear, pregnancy, cost) ~2.4. Adults ≈ 271M, so current users ≈ 70.2M (down from 74.8M), used-and-off ≈ 32.2M, never-used ≈ 168.6M. Age bands weighted by adult shares (20/33/24/23%): 3.0 + 9.17 + 9.36 + 4.37 = 25.9. Income thirds: (30.5 + 24.2 + 23.0)/3 = 25.9. The middle third fell most (28→24.2) as employer weight-management coverage retreated. The bottom third rose (21.7→23.0) through free generic semaglutide at HRSA sites and pharmacies for incomes under 250% FPL, plus $39–69 cash generics. The top third fell (34→30.5) but keeps the 30% molecule, retatrutide, through cash or diabetes codes. 65+ rose 17→19 (~11.8M) on the dementia label and $0-copay generic under the renewed Bridge; ~1.2M of them pay cash for generic to avoid the Bridge's DEXA and weigh-in conditions. 30–49 fell 31→27.8 as employer coverage went. Pediatric: 1.4% of ~73M ≈ 1.02M, ~190k aged 6–11, mostly generic semaglutide and liraglutide. The ~32M used-and-off adults are now the largest group that has to explain itself: mostly mid-income workers who lost coverage and did not move to cash, people locked out by conditioning, and GI quitters, many of them tort claimants.

access.public_coverage: Medicare: in Dec 2033 Congress renewed the GLP-1 Bridge through 2035 with generic semaglutide as the default. Medicare pays $45/month with a $0 copay. Brands (tirzepatide, retatrutide, amycretin) require step therapy and pay $199 with a $50 copay. The continuation conditions (≥5% at month 6, ≥80% PDC, DEXA and a resistance referral for 65+) are retained. Bridge obesity users ≈ 4.0M: 2.6M generic × $45 × 12 = $1.40B, plus 1.4M brand × $199 × 12 = $3.34B, ≈ $4.7B/yr, down from $9.2B with more people covered. Medicare overall pays ≈ 15.8% of adult users ≈ 11.1M (10.6M aged 65+ plus 0.5M disabled under 65), mostly through diabetes, CV and dementia-label Part D. Medicaid pays ≈ 13.5% ≈ 9.5M: 6.5M generic × $40 × 12 = $3.12B, plus 3.0M brand on diabetes codes × $180 × 12 = $6.48B, ≈ $9.6B combined federal and state. Seven states still run adherence waivers. HRSA Community Incretin Access Program, FY2034, $4.0B and still unconditional: free generic semaglutide at health centres and contracted pharmacies for incomes ≤250% FPL. It serves ≈7.0M: 6.0M generic semaglutide (weight, cessation, AUD) × $32 × 12 = $2.30B, plus 1.0M generic liraglutide × $45 × 12 = $0.54B, plus dispensing at $9 × 7.0M × 12 = $0.76B, ≈ $3.6B, with $0.4B for site staffing and DEXA access. TRICARE/VA/DoD ≈ 2.4M. Readiness programme ≈ 165k active duty: 95k generic × $32 × 12 = $36M, plus 70k tirzepatide × $149 × 12 = $125M, ≈ $161M.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Generic semaglutide is a commodity worldwide; India has 100+ brands at $5–30/month. Generic tirzepatide is sold in India, Brazil, Turkey and now Mexico and Egypt. Chinese triple agonists are approved domestically and exported to Southeast Asia and the Gulf. Retatrutide has no generic anywhere.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~70.2M adult users: commercial 26.1% (18.3M, of whom ~11M are on diabetes, CV, OSA or MASH codes and ~7.3M on weight-management benefits), Medicare 15.8% (11.1M), Medicaid 13.5% (9.5M), HRSA free 10.0% (7.0M), TRICARE/VA/DoD 3.4% (2.4M), cash/direct 26.2% (18.4M), gray 5.0% (3.5M) = 100%. Generic collapse: under 2033 patent-settlement dates, five ANDA holders and a Novo authorised generic were selling semaglutide pens by late 2033. Section 232 duty on Indian API adds ~$6–8/month, yet retail cash reached $49–69 by mid-2034, and Cost Plus and warehouse clubs sell at $39. TrumpRx tirzepatide fell $299→$249 and retatrutide $399→$349 under the Strategic Supply Agreement. Wegovy direct is $129, and its list price has been cut to $699. Retatrutide list stays $1,499. Employer retreat: after the July 2033 Sixth Circuit ruling against adherence-based premium differentials, employers lost their conditioning lever. Coverage for weight management fell from 63% to 41%. Retained coverage concentrates on diabetes, CV, OSA and MASH codes, and ~22% of employers now offer a flat $40–50/month HSA 'metabolic stipend' that pays for generic semaglutide, not retatrutide. The result is two tiers: a 30% molecule for those with a diabetes code, a plan or $349, and a ~15% molecule for everyone else. Gray users fell from 9M to 3.5M. 503A compounders lost their rationale once generics existed. The remaining gray trade is Indian and Turkish generic tirzepatide by mail and research-peptide retatrutide in gyms. Skip-but-fill has largely vanished from commercial plans but persists in the Bridge and the Medicaid waivers.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic; US generics and Novo authorised generic from 2033)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro; no US generic)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, obesity incl. 12 mg maintenance; type 2 diabetes from May 2033)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular co-agonist, weekly injectable (amycretin, approved Aug 2033)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 small-molecule, daily oral (orforglipron: Foundayo; BED low dose; nicotine dependence from Oct 2033)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide incl. US generics)
GLP-1 agonist / GIPR antagonist conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, obesity with MASH)
Activin type II receptor antibody + tirzepatide co-pack (bimagrumab + tirzepatide, approved Apr 2034 for adults ≥60 with obesity and low muscle mass)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: nicotine dependence including e-cigarettes and pouches, adults (orforglipron, Oct 2033; semaglutide cessation label extended to e-cigarettes, Oct 2033)
dementia-risk reduction ≥55 with T2D or obesity plus CVD (semaglutide)
sarcopenic obesity ≥60, muscle-preservation claim (bimagrumab + tirzepatide, Apr 2034)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: generic semaglutide for vaping cessation in 16–17-year-olds, prescribed by adolescent-medicine and school-linked clinics
'brain health' generic semaglutide in 50–64-year-olds without diabetes or CVD, now cheap enough to be cash-routine
retatrutide prescribed on 'prediabetes-adjacent' or borderline T2D coding to reach diabetes-code coverage, now subject to payer HbA1c audits
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The triple-agonist driver is met by retatrutide, which has been on the market since 2031 and now has a new indication. FDA approved it for type 2 diabetes in May 2033 on the TRANSCEND-T2D programme, putting the ~30% molecule onto the diabetes codes where employer coverage is concentrating. No new triple agonist reached the US. Chinese originator triples remain NMPA-only. Amycretin, under review at the start of the window, was approved in Aug 2033 (~22% at 68 weeks) and has had a modest launch. Bimagrumab + tirzepatide was filed in Mar 2032 and approved in Apr 2034, more than 12 months later, narrowly for adults ≥60 with obesity and low appendicular lean mass. Launch volume is small (~60k). The nicotine indication rests on a phase 3 orforglipron trial in combustible and e-cigarette users (continuous abstinence weeks 9–24 roughly 1.8× placebo), and Novo extended the semaglutide cessation label on supportive data. US generic semaglutide entered under 2033 settlement dates, with five ANDA holders plus a Novo authorised generic. Tirzepatide stays protected to the mid-2030s. US incretin net price fell ~35–40% across the window as semaglutide went generic, and volume fell ~6%.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Brand-to-generic switching produces a transient GI bump where pen dose increments differ, and rates remain highest on retatrutide 12 mg.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; FDA device-equivalence guidance for generic pens (2033).

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Mass-tort scale. MDL 3094 holds ~158,000 filed and tolled claims: ~118,000 gastroparesis, ileus and obstruction, ~34,000 pancreatitis and ~6,000 pancreatic cancer. The May 2034 settlement programme ($6.5B, ≈118k × ~$55k average, 95% participation threshold) covers brand-product GI claims only. Claimants injured on generic semaglutide face federal preemption of failure-to-warn claims against generic makers.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Nov 2033: FDA adds postmarketing reports of delayed gastric emptying persisting after discontinuation to the Adverse Reactions section, explicitly without a causal finding. Innovator-liability bills are introduced in California and Illinois.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Tracks speed of loss; highest on retatrutide.
Registries still show low absolute risk and no confirmed causation. The MDL track (~34k claims) is excluded from the settlement and heads to its own bellwethers in 2035.
Persists. Employer retreat removed commercial resistance-training conditions, so younger cash-generic users get no muscle support at all.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning stands. Bridge resistance referral is retained. Bimagrumab + tirzepatide approved Apr 2034 for ≥60 with low muscle mass.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Medicare hip-fracture admissions rose a further ~3% in 2032–33. Modelled excess ≈ 11.8M users 65+ × ~0.5%/yr × HR 0.35 ≈ 20,000/yr, concentrated in women and cyclers, and especially the ~1.2M 65+ cash-generic users outside DEXA conditions. Pediatric bone-accrual final study is due 2035.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: DEXA warning retained. A 2033 pediatric labelling update adds a bone-accrual precaution for use beyond 2 years.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; very low absolute risk.
No causal association, including in the nicotine-dependence trial population.
~10–15% of long-term users report reduced pleasure; ~8% vs ~4% clinically meaningful at high retatrutide doses. About 50% of long-term users report a deliberate dose holiday in the past year.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Retatrutide label and class precaution unchanged. The orforglipron nicotine label carries the same Adverse Reactions language.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The 2033–34 driver is coverage loss: ~4.5 pts of adults stopped when employer weight coverage ended, and only about half moved to cash generic.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No federal rule. Indiana waiver litigation unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Protein, iron, B12 and vitamin D signals persist and are worst among unsupported cash-generic users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance only outside the Bridge.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~12 years of adult follow-up. ~1.02M under-18s are on drug and ~190k aged 6–11. Pubertal-timing data are still absent. Cyclers are now 48% of ever-users.
Poison-centre incretin calls fell ~30% as compounded semaglutide disappeared. Residual harm comes from mail-order generic tirzepatide and gym research-retatrutide.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CBP seizures continue. 503A semaglutide compounding effectively ended once FDA confirmed no shortage and the generics launched.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg.
$39–69 generic semaglutide has made off-label 'brain health' use among 50–64-year-olds a cash habit outside any DEXA condition.
Driven by litigation advertising and stimulated FAERS reporting. Large pharmacoepidemiology cohorts are null so far, with short latency the main caveat.

safety_ledger.effect: Use in young nicotine-dependent adults and adolescents (vaping)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The cessation label has brought ~1.1M adults 18–29 onto drug, mostly lean or normal weight. Off-label 16–17 use is in the tens of thousands, and weight effects in non-obese young users are poorly characterised.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labels require BMI documentation and limit courses to 24 weeks. A pediatric study has been requested.

food_and_beverage.state: Packaged-food volume decline slows to ~1.5% a year as adoption dips and reaches a plateau. The cheap generic tier comes with no counselling, so protein formats grow among Bridge and HRSA users while cash-generic users eat less of the same food. Majors finish divesting snacks, and private-equity owners run them for cash. Convenience-store chains report nicotine and snack baskets shrinking together.

alcohol.state: Spirits and beer volume falls for a sixth year, though more slowly. The nicotine label adds a second front: cigarette volume fell ~9% in 2033–34 and vape and pouch volume ~6%. State tobacco-settlement (MSA) payments, which are indexed to cigarette shipments, are forecast to fall, and North Carolina and Kentucky budget offices now model an 'incretin cessation' line next to the excise one.

restaurants.state: Value chains keep consolidating. Fast casual has made the half plate standard. Normalisation means menus no longer advertise 'GLP-1 portions'; small portions are simply the default size.

apparel.state: Size runs are stable. The two-tier bodies show up in fit data: retailers in Dayton and Columbus report a 'stalled middle' of shoppers who lost coverage and partly regained.

fitness.state: Bridge referrals keep senior strength programmes full. Commercial referral-slip traffic fell after the employer retreat, and low-cost gym chains report flat memberships.

insurance.state: Employers have exited weight management and kept diabetes, CV, OSA and MASH coverage. Payers now audit diabetes coding as retatrutide prescribing migrates to T2D codes. PBMs' adherence-verification business shrank after the Sixth Circuit ruling. Pharmacy trend falls to ~+4% on generic semaglutide.

pharma.state: Semaglutide's US revenue has collapsed under generics. Novo is shrinking in the US, living on CagriSema and amycretin and paying duty. Lilly's retatrutide and tirzepatide carry the US market under the national-champion bargain. Generic makers (Teva, Viatris, Sandoz, Dr. Reddy's, Apotex) run thin margins on duty-bearing Indian API. MDL settlement reserves are booked.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on the drug is unremarkable, like wearing glasses. The body now signals which tier you are in. A 30% body, especially a trained one, signals retatrutide: a diabetes code, a good plan or $349. A 15% body signals generic semaglutide. A heavier body is the one that needs explaining, and people offer the explanation unprompted: lost coverage, GI, pregnancy, 'I'm one of the lawsuit people.'
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle remains the top marker. The new class line runs between molecules rather than between on and off. In Dayton's mid-size employers, warehouse and office staff who lost weight-management coverage in January 2034 moved to $49 generic, and coworkers can see who kept tirzepatide through a spouse's diabetes code.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Open Table suppers continue in Grand Rapids, Nashville and Tulsa but have shrunk. Their hosts now spend as much time explaining why they eat as celebrating it. Office lunches assume small appetites, and a person who finishes a full plate gets a glance rather than a remark.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles have stopped listing the molecule because everyone is on something. 'Off' is now a field people annotate: 'off for IVF', 'off, GI', 'off on principle'. Dose holidays around conception remain routine.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is treated as correctable, like eyesight. Unmedicated appetite is read as a choice, a lack of coverage, or a medical reason. The 'appetite liberty' laws in Tennessee and Idaho are still on the books, but the Sixth Circuit ruling made them largely moot.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. ~10–15% of long-term users report reduced pleasure across agents, and ~8% have clinically meaningful anhedonia at high retatrutide doses. About 50% of long-term users took a deliberate holiday in the past year, up from 45%. Cheap cash generic makes holidays easy: users simply stop buying for a month. Skip-but-fill persists mainly among Bridge and Medicaid-waiver users. The nicotine label added ~1.1M young adults whose complaint is a dual withdrawal: 'no vape, no grey-free days'. Low-dose Foundayo (BED, nicotine, 'quiet') has ~2.4M users.
interior_life.framing: A side effect everyone knows about and manages, like a hangover. 'The grey' is ordinary speech, and 'holiday' is now a verb. Clinicians say reward modulation. Cessation ads promise to 'turn down the pull', with the grey disclosed in small type.
interior_life.effect_on_work: After the Sixth Circuit ruling, employers no longer see adherence data, so whether someone is greyed out at work is a private matter. Sales staff still time holidays to quarter-end. Military and police programmes still track tape and DEXA, and chaplain reports of 'the grey' continue.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' billings are routine. A wave of vape-quitter stand-up treats the shot as the thing that killed the last fun habit. Casino and sports-betting handle growth stays below pre-incretin trend.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Holidays for anniversaries and conception are expected. Couples split across tiers (one on covered retatrutide, one on cash generic) report mismatched hunger and mismatched grey at the same table.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Free generic semaglutide is popular across party lines as cheap public health. Asking whether candidates are on the drug is passé; reporters now ask why a candidate is off. The backlash coalition has pivoted from conditioning, which it largely won in court, to 'pacification' attacks on HRSA, and tort-lawyer advertising is a political force. Tobacco-state legislators complain about lost settlement revenue.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access and now pro-generic. FDA cleared generic semaglutide pens with device-equivalence guidance, approved the nicotine, amycretin, retatrutide-T2D and bimagrumab decisions, and answers the GI tort with postmarketing language rather than restriction.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Direct free provision is the new centre of policy: HRSA's $4.0B FY2034 programme gives generic semaglutide free and unconditionally at health centres and contracted pharmacies to anyone ≤250% FPL. The Bridge was renewed with generic as the $0-copay default. The ACA cessation mandate is unchanged, and whether its two 90-day courses cover e-cigarette cessation is disputed among plans. No mandate to take the drug.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Employer conditioning was largely dismantled by the Jul 2033 Sixth Circuit ruling, and the other circuit case was stayed pending a cert petition. Public conditioning survives: the Bridge's 6-month response, PDC and DEXA rules, and seven Medicaid adherence waivers. The state that pays still watches; private employers have stopped watching.
state.workforce_or_military: The DoD Metabolic Readiness Program continues at ~165k active duty, generic semaglutide first and tirzepatide second. Body-composition separations remain ~30% below 2030. Religious-accommodation requests have reached ~3,400. Police and fire contracts in Phoenix, Houston and Chicago switched to generic.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The national-champion bargain is under strain: generic semaglutide made from duty-bearing Indian API undercuts the federal ceiling-price logic, and Lilly now holds its exemption mainly on tirzepatide and retatrutide. A WTO panel on India's Section 232 complaint was established in 2033. Novo's US footprint is shrinking. Mail-order generic tirzepatide from India and Turkey is the main CBP target.

events.event: Generic semaglutide pens launch in the US under patent-settlement entry dates as five ANDA holders and a Novo authorised generic enter at once. Retail cash falls below $75 by autumn and to $39–69 by mid-2034. Novo cuts Wegovy list to $699 and Lilly trims tirzepatide to $249 and retatrutide to $349.
FDA approves retatrutide for type 2 diabetes, putting the 30%-weight-loss triple agonist on diabetes codes that payers already cover. Within months PBMs launch HbA1c audits of new T2D diagnoses.

The Sixth Circuit rules that premium differentials based on PBM fill data do not satisfy wellness-program 'reasonable alternative standard' rules. Large employers respond by dropping weight-management coverage for 2034 while keeping diabetes, cardiac and sleep-apnea codes. Weight coverage falls from 63% to 41% of employers.

FDA approves orforglipron (Foundayo) for nicotine dependence including e-cigarettes and pouches, and extends semaglutide's cessation label to vaping. North Carolina and Kentucky budget offices cut tobacco-settlement revenue forecasts.

The omnibus funds HRSA's Community Incretin Access Program at $4.0B to provide free, unconditional generic semaglutide to anyone at or below 250% of poverty, and renews the Medicare Bridge through 2035 with a $0-copay generic default. The 'pacification' rider fails.

Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly announce a $6.5B settlement programme for about 118,000 gastroparesis, ileus and obstruction claims in MDL 3094. Pancreatitis and pancreatic-cancer tracks are excluded, and plaintiffs injured on generic semaglutide find preemption blocks their claims against generic makers.

open_tensions: Two tiers have hardened: a ~15% generic for everyone and a 30% triple agonist for those with diabetes codes, good plans or $349. Coding drift toward T2D is now an audit war between prescribers and PBMs, and tirzepatide patents run out only in the mid-2030s.

The settlement covers brand GI claims only. Pancreatitis bellwethers start in 2035, and generic-semaglutide users injured after 2033 cannot sue for failure to warn. Innovator-liability bills in California and Illinois would push brand makers to pay for generic harms.
Generic semaglutide on duty-bearing Indian API has hollowed out the national-champion bargain. The WTO panel, Novo's US retreat and the 2035 Bridge expiry all reopen who sets federal prices.

Free generic at HRSA sites and the nicotine label reach lean young adults and, off-label, teenagers, while state budgets lose tobacco-settlement revenue. The backlash calls it pacification, tobacco-state legislators call it a revenue hole, and its long-horizon effects in non-obese young bodies are unknown.
still_true: The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
The ACA preventive mandate still requires plans to cover semaglutide for smoking cessation in two 90-day courses a year.
No FDA-approved generic tirzepatide is sold in the US; tirzepatide remains patent-protected to the mid-2030s.
Tennessee's and Idaho's 'appetite liberty' laws barring employers from conditioning premiums on incretin use remain on the books.

The DoD Metabolic Readiness Program still offers tirzepatide or semaglutide through military treatment facilities to service members who fail body-composition standards, and separation for failing standards is not voluntary.

prose.headline: Forty-Nine Dollars and No Excuses: The Year Being Off the Shot Became the Thing You Have to Explain
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 about seventy million American adults take an incretin drug, roughly one in four. That is fewer than two years ago, even though the drug has never been cheaper. Generic semaglutide arrived in March 2033 on dates lawyers had settled years before. Five manufacturers and Novo's own authorised generic launched at once, and the price fell the way commodity prices fall. By summer a month's pen costs forty-nine dollars at a Kroger pharmacy and thirty-nine at a warehouse club. The Indian ingredient still pays a tariff, and the tariff adds about seven dollars.

The drop in users follows from the price drop. In July 2033 the Sixth Circuit ruled that employers could not set premiums using pharmacy fill records, which had become a fiction once users learned to collect refills they never injected. Without that lever, and with the drug now cheap enough to call affordable, employers simply stopped covering weight loss. Coverage fell from nearly two-thirds of employers to two-fifths. What remains attaches to diabetes, heart disease and sleep apnea. Many firms now give workers a flat forty-dollar stipend and wish them well. About half the people who lost coverage bought the generic. The other half stopped, and they are the new visible population: some thirty-two million adults who used the drug and are off it now.

The drug that matters most has not gone generic. Retatrutide, the triple agonist that takes off thirty percent of body weight, won a type 2 diabetes approval in May 2033. That put it inside the one door employers left open. The country now has two tiers: a fifteen-percent drug for everyone and a thirty-percent drug for people with a diabetes code, a good plan or three hundred and forty-nine dollars. Insurers audit new diabetes diagnoses, and doctors resent the audits.

Washington went the other way and made the cheap tier free. In December Congress funded health centres to hand out generic semaglutide, with no conditions, to anyone at or below two and a half times the poverty line. Seven million people take it that way, and the programme costs less than it did when it served half as many. The Medicare Bridge now defaults to generic at no copay, though it still drops people who do not lose five percent and still requires the bone scan. The poorest third of the country now uses the drug at nearly the same rate as the middle.

In October the FDA approved the daily pill for quitting nicotine, vapes and pouches included. Young adults who were never heavy are taking it to quit. Cigarette volumes have fallen sharply, and in Raleigh and Frankfort budget officers are rewriting the tobacco-settlement line that pays for children's programmes.

The lawsuits finally reached their size. More than a hundred and fifty thousand claims sit in the federal stomach-paralysis litigation. In May the two makers offered six and a half billion dollars to settle the gastroparesis and obstruction claims, but not the pancreatitis claims and not the pancreatic-cancer claims, for which the large studies find nothing so far. People hurt on the generic discovered that federal law largely shields generic makers from failure-to-warn suits. Late-night television runs one ad for the pill and the next for the lawyers.

The flatness people call the grey is still the common complaint, and the cheap price makes holidays easy: you skip a month of buying. Being on the drug is unremarkable, and profiles no longer mention it. The heavier body is the one that gets explained, often unprompted: lost coverage, stomach trouble, trying for a baby, principle. Open Table suppers still meet in Grand Rapids and Nashville, though fewer people come and more of the evening goes to explaining why they eat. From a distance the country looks settled. Up close it is sorted by molecule.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Dana Kowalczyk wakes at 5:10 in Kettering, Ohio, and checks the fridge door. Behind the mustard is the pen, the generic one in the grey box. It cost forty-nine dollars at Kroger, and the label is a company she had never heard of. Thursday is injection day. She clicks it into her thigh while the coffee runs.

Until January the pen was Zepbound and the dispatch company paid for it. Now there is a line on her pay stub that says METABOLIC STIPEND $40.00.

At the depot she runs routes for eleven trucks. Around ten she is hungry, really hungry, the way she hasn't been in three years. She eats an apple and then a second one.

Luis brings in donut holes for his birthday. Nobody takes more than one. Terri from billing, whose husband's diabetes got her onto the triple, has lost so much weight that her lanyard swings. "You still on the cheap stuff?" she asks kindly. Dana says she's thinking about it.

At lunch she watches a TV mounted above the microwave. A woman in an ad holds a pill and says turn down the pull. The next ad asks if you have suffered stomach paralysis.

After work she picks up her son Caleb, sixteen. The car smells of mango vapor. She says nothing. The school nurse sent a pamphlet: free cessation pill, ask your clinic, parental consent required.

Dinner is chicken thighs and rice. Her husband Marcus eats half, as he always does now. Dana finishes her plate and then sits there with the empty plate, and nobody says anything.
